summary: Lane County, OR: 40-ft wooden L-4 tower built 1954-55 on Canton Point; abandoned 1973 or removed 1976 per sources; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 40-foot wooden L-4 tower with a Douglas fir lookout house
facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1973 per firelookout.com; removed in 1976 per Forest Lookouts. No source describes the site today

staffing.status: a Portland State graduate from Eugene was stationed there in July 1963; abandoned 1973 per firelookout.com

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com says abandoned in 1973; Forest Lookouts says removed in 1976. Both dates are kept as separate events, and the story reports the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: The brief's record is accurate on kind, height (12.2 m is 40 ft), county and status. Two sources give different end dates (abandoned 1973 per firelookout.com; removed 1976 per Forest Lookouts), and the story reports both. The 1954 News-Review item quoted on Forest Lookouts is the only detailed description of construction. The August 1962 News-Review item about four summers in the Umpqua lookout service is headed Canton Point but does not clearly say the man worked there, so it is left out. No current source was found on what remains or on access; a Forest Service removal record or a Lane County newspaper search for 1973-76 would be the next steps. No corrections proposed.
